searchText: When it says "read only" does that mean you can't send transactions? right, have to change that, it's meant to say "non-validator" - ie you can do all the normal execution chain stuff Sorry, is this the right channel for this question? 16K https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md Yes, thank you <@602753420033785856> ! Had a question about `finalized`, the part thats confusing me is that lets say Epoch `147196` is `finalized`, it consists of slots `4,710,272` to `4,710,303`…if I call `beacon/blocks/finalized` to get the latest finalized slot it returns `4,710,272` which is the first slot in that epoch, shouldn't it return the last slot if the whole epoch is considered `finalized`? No, afaik the state at the slot you get returned is finalized. Not anything after. This is often the block of the first slot of an epoch, but doesn't have to be (could also be a block in the previous epoch). I guess my new question is “what does a finalized epoch mean”? I would assume (seemingly incorrectly) that the slots in that epoch are themselves finalized. I guess that's how I would interpret that as well. Your endpoint though is not asking for the last finalized epoch, it's asking for the last finalized block/state/etc. And it returns that correctly. Correct if you get the latest finalized epoch or look on https://beaconscan.com/ the slot that is shown as finalized is the first slot in the finalized epoch. The specs do not have a notion of an Epoch being finalized. We finalize `Checkpoints` these are a pair `(Root, Epoch)` of a root of a block, and an epoch. It is required that the corresponding block, with root `Root` is the highest block with slot lower or equal to `32*Epoch`. Every ancestor of that block is finalized and that block itself a block is an ancestor of itself but yeah yeah I guess there's no formal definition of ancestor in the spec but right, any block in the canonical chain before or equal to the block is finalized In the example above, the block at slot 4,710,272 has slot exactly equal to 32*147196, therefore can be used as a root for a checkpoint with epoch 147196, any ancestor of it (itself included) is final, and the descendants not necessarily until we finalize another checkpoint in the future Ok so my mental model was incorrect then which was what I assumed when I posed the question. Thank you for explaining

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: The specs do not have a notion of an Epoch being finalized. We finalize `Checkpoints` these are a pair `(Root, Epoch)` of a root of a block, and an epoch. It is required that the corresponding block, with root `Root` is the highest block with slot lower or equal to `32*Epoch`. Every ancestor of that block is finalized
